approachQuestion.prompt:
Revise a Printed Label

A lowercase ASCII string text is accompanied by k edit records (start,length,replacement), sorted by strictly increasing start. Each edit removes length characters beginning at start in the ORIGINAL text, then puts replacement there. Return the final text with all edits applied simultaneously. Edits are guaranteed valid and non-overlapping. Characters outside the edited ranges keep their order.

Example 1: text = "abcdef", edits = [(1,2,"x"),(4,1,"pq")] → "axdpqf".
Example 2: text = "abcd", edits = [(0,2,""),(2,2,"z")] → "z".
Example 3: text = "cab", edits = [] → "cab".

Constraints:
1 ≤ n = text.length ≤ 200,000; 0 ≤ k ≤ n.
Each start is a zero-based index; length ≥ 1; start+length ≤ n.
For consecutive records, previous.start+previous.length ≤ next.start. Adjacent ranges are legal.
Replacement strings contain only a–z and may be empty. Their total length R is at most 200,000.
Do not modify text or the edit records. Return one new flat string.

options.text: Compute the final length from n and the edit lengths. Allocate a character buffer of exactly that length. Walk edits in order: copy the untouched original span, then its replacement, and move the source position past the removed range. Copy the final untouched suffix and convert the buffer to a flat string.
options.feedback: All source positions refer to the unchanged original. Removed ranges are skipped once, and output is written in order without rebuilding earlier output.

options.text: Create a separate full copy of text as a character array. Then compute the final length, allocate an output buffer, and fill it from the copied source and replacements using the same ordered span walk; convert the output buffer to a flat string.
options.feedback: The result is correct for every legal edit list, but the full source copy is unnecessary. The immutable original already supplies all untouched characters.

options.text: Start with a mutable copy of text. Process edits from left to right, removing and inserting at each record’s original start index in the currently changed text.
options.feedback: Earlier replacements can shift later positions. In Example 1, after the first edit the text is "axdef"; index 4 now identifies f rather than the original e.

options.text: For each edit, take the original substring to be removed and replace its first occurrence anywhere in the current text with the replacement.
options.feedback: Positions matter even when substrings repeat. For text="aba", edits=[(2,1,"z")], the result must be "abz", but first-occurrence replacement produces "zba".

feedback.reason: All edit coordinates refer to the unchanged original label.
details: Compute the final output length. Allocate one buffer of exactly that length. Copy untouched original spans and replacement characters in edit order, skipping removed original ranges. Finish the suffix and convert the buffer to the returned flat string.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Fill a Sized Character Buffer”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let L=n−sum(length)+R be the returned string length. Reading a length, an edit field, or one character costs constant time. Allocating the buffer, writing it, and converting it to a flat string each cost O(L+1); conversion copies rather than transferring the buffer. The buffer is therefore auxiliary storage. Exclude the input and returned string, but include all helpers and stack. No recursion, hashing, dynamic append or temporary substring copies are used. Express the tight bound in k and L.
constraints: Each start is a zero-based index; length ≥ 1; start+length ≤ n.
For consecutive records, previous.start+previous.length ≤ next.start. Adjacent ranges are legal.
Replacement strings contain only a–z and may be empty. Their total length R is at most 200,000.
Do not modify text or the edit records. Return one new flat string.

options.text: O(k + L + 1) time, O(L + 1) auxiliary space.
O(n + R + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
O(k + L + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
O((k + 1)*(n + R + 1)) time, O(n + R + 1) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Visit edit records and surviving output characters, retaining a separate output-sized buffer.
details: Two passes over edit records compute the length and locate spans. The method reads and writes only characters that survive plus replacement characters, totaling L; it skips removed ranges by index arithmetic. Allocation and the final copy cost O(L+1). The separate character buffer remains auxiliary because conversion copies it into the returned string.
The option “O(k + L + 1) time, O(L + 1) auxiliary space.”: Every edit is inspected, every output character is written, and the separate buffer has L slots.
The option “O(n + R + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: This is not the tight output-sensitive bound when a long removed range is skipped, and it omits the buffer.
The option “O(k + L + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Excluding the returned string does not exclude the distinct buffer used to construct it.
The option “O((k + 1)*(n + R + 1)) time, O(n + R + 1) auxiliary space.”: Repeated whole-string rebuilding could incur such work, but the fixed method fills one buffer once.
